findings.evidence: 1. List the candidate causal changes. 2. Rank them by observable consequence and evidence strength
findings.fix: Merge steps 1-3 into one line, for example 'Pick the change with the strongest observable consequence and a defensible counterfactual'. The model already lists and ranks candidates without being told. Keep steps 4-5, which hold the expert checks.

findings.evidence: Use when users ask what they learned, want an engineering takeaway, or reflect on recent commits, a branch diff, a specific commit, or staged/unstaged changes
findings.fix: Use when the user asks what they learned, wants an engineering takeaway or retrospective, or reflects on a merged PR, a feature branch, recent commits, a specific commit, or staged, unstaged or untracked changes, even without naming Git or a principle. Grounds one lesson in the actual diff, names a design principle only when the evidence supports it, and gives a next-time practice. Not for generic engineering tutorials, bug reviews, commit messages, release notes or planning a refactor.

findings.evidence: "find all TODO comments in this repository" / "explain this algorithm line by line"; evals.json has no case for a merge commit or for a missing base branch
findings.fix: Replace the two keyword-free negatives with near-misses, for example 'write a postmortem for last night's outage from the incident channel' or 'what changed between v2.3 and v2.4? list it for the changelog'. Add an output eval with a merge-commit `git show` fixture that asserts the agent uses --first-parent and does not report an empty change.

findings.evidence: | On the base branch, or last N commits | `git log -p --first-parent -n <N>` (default N=5) |
findings.fix: Give the base branch an explicit rule for a dirty tree. For example: 'On the base branch with uncommitted or ?? work, use working changes first and include the last N commits only if the user asks about commits.' Today 'If there are no commits in scope, use working changes' never fires on main, because the last 5 commits are always in scope, so today's uncommitted work gets ignored.

findings.evidence: `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, and every `??` path from `git status`
findings.fix: Run `git status --short -uall`, or list the files under any `??` entry that ends in `/`. Plain status collapses a new directory into one `?? dir/` line, so following the step as written reads a directory path and misses the new files inside it.
